ActionListParams.description: `action/list` (Appendix E8): a session's actions, or an agent's.

env.description: Absent when a driver reports it; the runtime sets it.

hint.description: How to install a driver egg, when the runtime has none.

answers.description:
The answer to each of a request's `questions`, by question id: a choice id, a label, a
list of them, or text.

Answerable.description: Who can still answer once things go away. `process` was removed (Appendix E8).

message.description: The user item id for turn actions (Appendix E4).

request.description: The driver key of the request.

message.description: The id the user item gets.

deny.description: Paths the harness must not reach.

BlobPutParams.description: One chunk of a transfer between runtimes, at most 1 MiB (spec 24.2, E9).

target.description: The JSON Schema of the carrier's target.
Validated against the carrier's target schema.

fallback.description: Tried in order when this one fails.

CarrierRef.description: How a runtime reaches a peer.

tags.description: Semantic tags, separated by spaces: `plan`, `bypass`, `ask`, `read-only` and so on.

harness.description: The harness's own value, when it differs from `name`.

ConnectionGrant.description: The `connection` of `InitializeResult`: who the caller is and what it may do.

Containment.description: Whether the carrier's credentials reach more of the peer than its link endpoint (spec 24.4).

CorrelateFile.description:
`correlate.kdl`: per item kind, how items of two sources match and which source wins
(spec 32.1).

match.description: The keys tried in order: `ref` (the harness id), `position` (turn and order), `text`.

prefer.description: The source that wins while the binding runs.

history.description: The source that wins when history is read again.

compare.description: Fields compared in shadow mode; all of `set` when empty.

CorrelateKind.description:
`kind "tool" { match "ref" "position"; prefer "native"; history "transcript"; }`. `kind "*"`
covers the kinds not named.

DependsOnData.description: `depends-on "<option>" { when "<value>" { choice ... } }`; `when "*"` matches any other value.

DiscoveredSession.description: A harness session no Parrot session has.

Empty.description: The `{}` result of methods that return nothing; unknown fields are kept.

session.description: The session the call is for; the runtime sets it on calls it forwards.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for an approval, capped by the harness's tool-call timeout (27.2).

FunctionCallParams.description: `function/call`, from a client to the runtime and from the runtime to the providing client.

name.description: Namespaced, dot-separated; `parrot.` is reserved for this spec (27.1).

level.description: The lowest permission level that allows a call without asking (E5).

FunctionInfo.description: A function with its provider: `runtime`, a connection id or a link id.

FunctionResult.description:
The result of `function/call`, from the runtime to a client and from a provider to the
runtime.

name.description: Namespaced, dot-separated; `parrot.` is reserved for this spec (27.1).

level.description: The lowest permission level that allows a call without asking (E5).

HistoryReadResult.description: The stored history as updates; each has `binding: ""` (Appendix E4).

kind.description: Required on the first patch; never changes.

removed.description: Always `true` when present: the item is gone.

level.description: `level "read" { tool "Read"; tool "mcp__*"; }`. A tool in no level is `host`.

map.description:
`map level="write" network=#false { when permissionMode="acceptEdits"; }`, first match
wins. Several `when` nodes are alternatives; the properties of one must all hold. A
combination no `map` matches is `host` with network.

pin.description: Arguments that pin the harness's settings sources under a ceiling.

LevelsFile.description:
`levels.kdl`: the tools each level allows, and the level each combination of option values
gives (spec 15.2, Appendix E4).

tool-timeout.description:
`tool-timeout 60`: how many seconds the harness waits for one tool call, MCP calls
included. Calls into Parrot return before it, less a margin.

carrier.description: Absent if this runtime only accepts.

grant.description: What the peer may do here.

via.description: The carrier instance of the current connection.

code.description:
A pairing code from the peer's `link/invite`; without it, the runtime pairs over the
carrier with `ask`.

LinkAsk.description: The grant and offer `link/add` asks the peer for when it pairs over the carrier (spec 24.3).

authorizedKey.description:
Set when the peer's SSH key was written to `authorized_keys` restricted to
`parrot connect --link`: the peer then sees its link as `restricted` (spec 24.4).

code.description: The one-time pairing code. It is a secret: shown once, never logged.

env.description: Whether the peer sees this environment and its agents, and may create sessions in it.

LinkOffer.description: What a runtime shows a linked peer.

key.description: The peer's X25519 public key, in hex.

LinkPeer.description: The other runtime of a link, pinned at pairing.

MovedData.description: `data` of `-32050`: the runtime that owns the session now.

OfferedSessions.description:
Which sessions a link's peer sees. `linked`: only sessions created over the link or moved
here over it, with their descendants.

type.description: The JSON type of a free value, such as `string`, when there are no choices.

harness.description: The harness's own name for the option, such as a config key or a flag.

dynamic.description: The harness reports the choices at runtime; these are the fallback.

OptionData.description: `option "<id>" role= label= applies= default= { choice ...; depends-on ... }`.

OptionsFile.description: `options.kdl`: options the harness doesn't report itself (spec 15.1, 31).

action.description: The well-known action that produced the item, such as `continue`.

PermissionLevel.description: What an agent can do without asking anyone, lowest first.

Pin.description: Hold the harness to at most this level.

PinArgs.description: `pin { arg "--setting-sources" "" }`: the arguments to pass, in order.

multiSelect.description: Whether more than one option may be picked.

options.description: The options to pick from; empty for free text.

Question.description: One question of a request that asks several (spec 14).

Ref.description: A harness's own reference to a session, item or request.

session.description: Omitted when a driver reports the request.

path.description: Sessions from the root to this one; omitted by drivers.

questions.description:
A request with several questions: one entry per question, answered by id in
`Answer.answers`. Absent for a single question, which uses `choices`.

RunStatus.description: The status of `script`, `subagent`, `command`, `file_change` and `web` items (Appendix E8).

code.description: Absent when the harness doesn't expose it.

runtime.description: The owning runtime: where the current binding runs.

at.description: A turn id; the latest when left out.

summary.description: `none` or `source`; `source` asks the source to summarize itself and needs `delegate`.

SessionCommitParams.description: The second phase of a move (E9): keyed and idempotent.

SessionConfigureParams.description: `session/configure` (Appendix E8): `delegate` on a subtree, `manage` on a root.

text.description: Text to type, as if pasted.

press.description: Named keys to press in order, such as `enter`, `tab` or `ctrl-c`.

SessionKeysParams.description: `session/keys` (Appendix E4): text and named keys for a binding under TUI control.

workspace.description: Required, unless a `seed` that carries the workspace gives one (23.1).

prompt.description: A first prompt, queued once the binding starts; saves a round trip and an empty session.

record.description: The session as the owner stores it.

workspace.description: The session's workspace; `transfer` names its blob when it travels.

log.description: The transfer that carries the session's items.

SessionOfferParams.description: The first phase of a move (E1): the owner offers a session to the target.

binding.description: The binding the target started idle.

control.description:
Switch the binding to the other control (32.2). The harness session isn't resumed across
the switch, so its history travels as a bundle (23.2).

SessionRef.description: Params of methods that take only `{ session }`: `session/get`, `session/delete`.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, so a list can show or filter by it without `session/get`.

workspace.description: The workspace the session works in.

SessionSummary.description: What lists and the index feed carry.

SubagentItem.description: A subagent. Drivers report `key` (30.3); the runtime fills `session`.

anyOf.description: A session and its descendants in one stream.

TaskAssignResult.description: The result of `task/assign`: the session's new `Task`.

task.description: The session's `Task` as it is now.

output.description: Structured when the task has a `result` schema, else `{ text }`.

result.description: A JSON Schema the output must match.

TaskStatus.description: A task's status as summaries carry it. `interrupted` comes from Appendix E7.

since.description: A cursor from an earlier call; the first call leaves it out.

timeout.description: Seconds, capped by the harness's tool-call timeout (20.1).

sessions.description: Limits the token to these sessions' subtrees.

provides.description: Patterns of the functions the token may provide.

Token.description: A client token for WebSocket connections (spec 3.4, Appendix E8).

binding.description: Omitted when a driver reports the turn.

oneOf.description: The pinned functions changed, so an MCP listing built from them is stale (spec 26).

seq.description: The update's place in the runtime's sequence; an opaque cursor (Appendix E2).

runtime.description: The runtime that emitted it (Appendix E2).

update.description: Unknown update types are kept raw and ignored.

countedIn.description: For embedded sessions: the session whose usage already includes this.

message.description: Set by a driver when the item echoes a runtime prompt (Appendix E4).

owner.description: The session that created a worktree.

WorkspaceReceiveParams.description: What a peer's `workspace/transfer` sends: unpack the transfer as a new workspace here.
